definitions.explanation: The son of one's brother or sister. The 〜っ{子|こ} ending adds warmth and is the form most people use in conversation, especially when the nephew is still a child.

examples.japanese: {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれた→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧。
{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{誕生日|たんじょうび}→誕生日：02910_tanjoubi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦プレゼント→プレゼント：01791_purezento⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{送|おく}った→送る：00742_okuru⟧。
examples.english: I sent my nephew a birthday present.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{遊|あそ}び→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{来|き}て→来る：00254_kuru⟧、⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦にぎやか→にぎやか：00873_nigiyaka⟧になった。
examples.english: My nephew came to visit at New Year's and the house got lively.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}まれる→生まれる：00905_umareru⟧: to have a nephew born
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}る→面倒を見る：18263_mendouwomiru⟧: to look after one's nephew
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{年玉|としだま}→お年玉：08452_otoshidama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげる→あげる：00546_ageru⟧: to give one's nephew New Year's money

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{甥|おい}→甥：13525_oi⟧: nephew — the plain term; used in writing and formal speech, where {甥|おい}っ{子|こ} would sound too cosy
- ⟦{姪|めい}っ{子|こ}→姪っ子：30761_meikko⟧: niece — the matching form
- ⟦{孫|まご}→孫：03731_mago⟧: grandchild — often mentioned alongside when talking about the younger generation

The same 〜っ{子|こ} pattern appears in words like ⟦{江戸|えど}→江戸：19369_edo⟧っ{子|こ} (a born-and-bred Tokyoite), where it likewise marks familiarity rather than small size.
